body:
The objection slot was absent this round, so the only critical pressure on the account comes from the rival. That changes what continuation means here: I am weighing the account against the rival, not triangulating three voices, and an objection neither document anticipated may still be out there.

What I accept from the rival: its core criticism stands. The account moved from 'no shared record' to 'make a shared record' as if the diagnosis were established, and the material — three flatmates, recurring arguments, later disagreement about what agreements meant, changing schedules, one friend withdrawing — does not establish it. The three readings now on the table (memory gap, scope divergence at the moment of agreement, arguments as standing-negotiation) are live and underdetermined. I also adopt the rival's reframing of the conversation with the avoiding friend: asking to hear their view of the group conversations rather than asking why they avoid them. On this point the two documents already converge — the account flagged the one-to-one approach as its own most contestable move — so I treat the reframing as settled, while noting that agreement between two documents is not evidence from the household.

Where I push back on the rival, in its favor: the rival worries that its own probe is compromised because recollection is exactly what is in dispute. That objection overreaches. The probe's value does not depend on anyone remembering accurately; it depends on the structure of the disagreement between reports. If each person's account of past agreements diverges at the same joint — always scope, or always recurrence, or always timing — that pattern is informative even if every report is wrong. I would also refine the rival's other interpretive branch: non-clustering answers are not one thing. Divergence that consistently favors the speaker, each person remembering the agreement as lighter for them, points toward the standing or fairness reading; divergence that looks like noise may mean the agreements were genuinely chaotic, or that the probe simply failed. So the probe needs its interpretive rule stated before it is run, and with only a few incidents across three people, any result is soft. Revised this way, the probe survives its author's own objection, and I would run it.

Where the criticism converts rather than defeats: the rival argues that a written record does not settle scope, recurrence, or role-versus-one-off, and may just relocate the argument onto the record. True — and that is the record's real function, stated as an objection. A note written at the moment of agreement, where all three can see it, forces the ambiguity into the open at the only moment it can be resolved cheaply: when B reads 'A: dishes, weekly' and says 'no, it was this week,' the disagreement happens now rather than next month. So the account's remedy survives, but its warrant changes from archive to forcing device, which changes the design: task, scope, recurrence, by-when, and what done means, stated aloud and written down together at the moment of agreement — not a ledger maintained afterward.

On the standing-negotiation reading I stay open, but I put it to work as the fallback hypothesis with its own observable signature. If the probe and the visible-note practice are tried and the arguments migrate onto the record itself — disputes about what done means, about who wrote what, about who is on it — that migration is exactly what the standing reading predicts, and the right move then is the rival's group-level one: name the pattern without blame ('we keep having this conversation; what is it protecting?') and take seriously that the disagreement may not be about chores at all.

Sequencing, which is what the original question actually asked for: the probe goes first because it alone requires no buy-in. It asks nothing of the household — only of the person asking, once per flatmate, including the avoiding friend on the reframed terms. The note practice and any check-in require all three to opt in, and the material gives no evidence they will. The account's weekly check-in I demote: its one solid footing in the stated facts is that schedules genuinely change, so a brief recurring moment to disclose changes before they bite has independent support — but I would not lead with it or make anything else conditional on it. Whether the friend answers the reframed probe at all also gives a provisional read on the account's unresolved question of whether the three can talk without a mediator — only about that channel, and provisional.

What I reject or set aside: the account's pairing of record and check-in as co-equal remedies; the rival's flat claim that non-clustering answers straightforwardly weaken the recording hypothesis (too coarse, per above); and any framing that treats the avoidance as a defect to correct before the probe returns. Load distribution, escalation, and the history of the avoidance remain undecided by anything in either document, and by nothing I can add.
commitments:
Taking this up means holding several separately revisable positions, and I want to say which are claims, which are proposals, and what would count against each.

First, an inherited-framework commitment: I adopt the account's memory-readings and the rival's two additions (scope divergence at the moment of agreement; arguments as standing-negotiation) as a set of live, underdetermined hypotheses. I also treat the rival's criticism of the account's diagnosis-to-remedy slide as a sound criticism of the account's reasoning — not as a refutation of the account's remedy, which I keep under a different warrant. If further material showed the real friction to be load inequality or a two-person conflict expressed through chores, the whole framing, my synthesis included, should be dropped.

Second, the lead proposal is the revised probe: ask each flatmate separately what they thought a past agreement covered, with the interpretive rule fixed in advance — clustering around scope, recurrence, or timing supports the recording or scope readings; directionally self-serving divergence supports the standing reading; shapeless divergence licenses no inference. This revises both parents: against the rival's self-objection, I claim the probe's evidential value rests on divergence structure rather than recollection accuracy; against the rival's interpretive branch, I claim non-clustering splits into at least two cases with different implications. That claim is contestable on grounds a critic could press now: the question itself primes the categories, so apparent clustering could be an artifact of phrasing, and the sample is at most a handful of incidents. Taking up the probe means accepting that risk and refusing to count ambiguous returns for or against any reading.

Third, the visible-note practice is adopted with its warrant changed from archive to forcing device, and with its content specified — scope, recurrence, by-when, doneness — precisely because the rival's relocation objection identifies where an underspecified note fails. The objection is inherited as a design constraint, not overcome. I am committed in advance to reading dispute-migration onto the record as evidence for the standing hypothesis and against my own sequencing, not as teething trouble.

Fourth, on the avoiding friend: I adopt the rival's reframed conversation, which inherits the unestablished reading that avoidance responds to being unheard in the group; both documents flagged this channel as weak, so my adoption rests on their convergence plus my own judgment, not on new evidence. Increased withdrawal after the conversation counts against the framing, mine included, and should not be redescribed as resistance.

Fifth, the check-in is demoted to optional and grounded only in the stated fact that schedules change; proposing a disclosure moment commits me to nothing further, and if it is experienced as an extra chore or as surveillance, that weighs against the whole systematizing direction I have endorsed here.

Open and unowned: load distribution, escalation, the history and cause of the avoidance, willingness to formalize, the soft evidential weight of any probe result, and the absence this round of an independent objection — the rival carried all critical weight, so my synthesis inherits whatever blind spot the two documents share. What I propose to take up is the sequence itself — probe first because it needs no buy-in, moment-of-agreement notes next, check-in optional, standing reading as fallback with migration as its tell — as an inquiry plan whose failure signatures are stated in advance, not as advice whose correctness I claim.
